description: Tucked into the hill country around Winchester, Tennessee, Five or Better Archery operates as a volunteer-run club affiliated with the ASA circuit, putting it on the map for archers chasing 3D competition and casual weekend practice alike. Volunteer clubs like this one tend to run lean, with members pitching in on course upkeep and event days rather than paid staff, so hours and walk-in access can vary by season and shoot schedule. If you're new to the area or new to ASA-style shooting, reaching out ahead of a visit is the smart move, since volunteer boards are usually happy to point newcomers toward the next scheduled shoot or work day.

Missoula sits at the junction of five river valleys, and Five Valleys Archery Club takes its name from that same geography, running a 3D course for members who'd rather stalk foam targets through western Montana terrain than stand at a flat line. As a club-run operation, it leans on member involvement more than a storefront business would, which usually means seasonal hours tied to daylight and course maintenance rather than a fixed schedule. Bowhunters in the Missoula area often use clubs like this to dial in shot placement before elk season. Contact the club directly for current membership terms and course access.

The 3D range gives bowhunters a place to practice on realistic target angles ahead of Florida's deer and hog seasons, distinct from a flat paper range. Being a club rather than a commercial storefront, it likely runs on membership dues and volunteer range officers rather than drop-in retail hours. Anyone in the Bunnell or Flagler County area looking to join should contact the club to confirm current membership and course access.

Flat Shootin Archery in Tollesboro is one of the volunteer-run clubs that keeps Kentucky's ASA 3D archery scene alive outside the bigger cities, hosting foam-target courses for members training toward regional and state shoots. Volunteer clubs in this network typically post their shoot calendar rather than keeping storefront hours, so the course opens around scheduled events and work days more than a fixed weekly schedule. For a bowhunter or 3D competitor in the Tollesboro area, this is the kind of low-key club where reputation and word of mouth matter more than marketing. Reach out to the club directly to find the next shoot date or ask about joining.

Archers passing through Flathead Valley or new to the area are better served calling ahead than showing up unannounced. It's the kind of club built around a tight-knit local membership rather than a walk-in commercial operation, so a direct conversation goes a long way.

Spring Branch sits in the Texas Hill Country, and Fletcha Brothers Archery Club is part of the ASA-affiliated network of volunteer clubs that keeps 3D archery active across that region. Run by members rather than paid staff, clubs like this typically schedule shoots and work days around the calendar rather than keeping fixed hours, so a course that's open one weekend may be closed the next. That combination, 3D and field archery side by side with instruction, is more than a lot of volunteer clubs offer, and it suggests an active membership base that maintains more than one style of shooting. Bowhunters and target archers in the Flint and Grand Blanc corridor have real reason to look this one up. Contact the club directly for lesson scheduling and membership details.

Alongside JOAD, the club also runs 3D archery and offers lessons, giving it a rare split identity between structured youth Olympic-style coaching and the more freeform 3D bowhunting-adjacent format. For a family in southeast Iowa looking to get a kid started in target archery, or an adult wanting instruction, this is a stronger-than-average find. Reach out to the club for JOAD enrollment windows, 3D course access, and lesson availability.
